resources.string: PrivacyKit has no format for this identifier yet, so it cannot generate one. Enter a value with the same shape as the real one, or leave the rule on Real.
This value must keep exactly the same length as the real one or apps discard it, and only the system can see that length. Use Static instead: the system generates it correctly there.

Build and OS fields are never randomised one at a time. A random model next to a real manufacturer is an impossible device, and that is easier to fingerprint than not spoofing at all. Use a device template, which sets all eight Build fields to one real, consistent device.
These get a brand new value on this app profile. This cannot be undone, and any Custom value you typed yourself is replaced.

%1$d identifiers you have configured are left exactly as they are: Per launch, Daily and Empty rules, the privacy restrictions, and identifiers PrivacyKit has no format for. Anything still set to Real is never touched.

%1$d of the 8 Build fields are spoofed on this app. They are excluded here on purpose: randomising them separately builds a device that cannot exist, which makes the app easier to fingerprint, not harder.
Also set all 8 Build fields to one real device: %1$s

Randomise all only regenerates identifiers that are already set to Static or Custom and that PrivacyKit has a format for. Nothing on this app profile matches yet. Set an identifier to Static or Custom first, and use a device template for the Build fields.
